description.narrative: The Pacific Islands Emergency Management Alliance (PIEMA) 2023-2028 is supported by Australia and New Zealand, managed by the Pacific Community (SPC). The Project is implementing activities that support the Regional Pacific Agenda and works with the key emergency management agencies to build better collaboration, strengthen communication and ultimately increase effectiveness when responding to disasters, under the lead of National Disaster Management Offices.

description.narrative: Australia’s support for the Pacific Islands Emergency Management Alliance is building the capacity of Pacific first responders. In April and May 2024, 30 participants from the Kiribati Police Fire Services (KPS) and Aviation Rescue and Fire undertook training supported by South Australia Country Fire Service and the KPS and Office of the President. The activity strengthens Kiribati emergency and disaster response capability as well as fire and rescue capability for structural, rural and aviation purposes. At the end of the training, two fire trucks were handed over to KPS as a donation from the Government of Australia

In 2017, Abdul Hakim joined Fiji’s National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) as a Training Officer, bringing with him 15 years’ of public service experience. Through the Pacific Islands Emergency Management Alliance (PIEMA), he completed several trainings including Pacific Incident Management Systems (PacIMS) Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) Awareness in 2019, and Training of Trainers (ToT) in Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Micro-qualifications in 2025. “Through the (PIEMA) training, I gained hands-on experience, and I learned to deliver scenario-based exercises effectively. This exposure not only enhanced my technical skills but also built my confidence in facilitating and coordinating training sessions,” Abdul shared. At the NDMO, Abdul began tailoring DRM training using real-world examples, simplifying complex concepts for rural communities, and implementing post-training evaluations to ensure impact. Now serving as a Training Facilitator with Fiji’s Ministry of Civil Service, Abdul incorporates risk-informed approaches and participatory techniques into national-level public service training. In a recent induction program, he used interactive methods from PIEMA’s ToT module to boost engagement and retention. Abdul’s journey shows how disaster risk management skills extend beyond emergency response - contributing to public sector leadership and coordination, across Fiji.

Luka Selu began his public service career in 2017 as a Community Officer, engaging island communities on climate change and disaster risk. When Tuvalu’s NDMO was established in 2019, he joined as a Disaster Relief and Recovery Officer, quickly stepping into a demanding role supporting disaster-affected populations across Tuvalu’s scattered islands and atolls. In 2020, Luka participated in PIEMA’s online Pacific Incident Management System (PacIMS) and Emergency Operations Centres (EOC) training. He also led a series of activities for developing Tuvalu’s Strategic Roadmap for Emergency Management (SREM). These activities strengthened his technical skills, regional networks, and leadership capacity. Today, at 30, Luka serves as the Director of NDMO Tuvalu—the youngest NDMO head in the Pacific. He has led national response efforts where he applied PacIMS principles during real emergencies and coordinated successful trainings and simulations like Exercise Longreach in 2025. Luka credits PIEMA for “exposure on every aspect of Emergency Management.” ‍ His story shows that when motivated individuals like Luka are supported with targeted training and regional networks, they can grow into national and regional leaders—building resilient institutions while shaping disaster management across the Pacific.
